title: SwiftUI data flow: @State, @Binding, @Observable, @Environment
summary: Choose the wrapper by asking "who owns this data?". `@State` owns it, `@Binding` borrows it with write access, `@Environment` receives it from far above, `@Bindable` makes bindings to an observable model.
body: **In simple words:** SwiftUI views are recreated all the time, so normal `var`s would be reset. Property wrappers tell SwiftUI to keep data in its own storage and to refresh the view when it changes.

**The modern set (iOS 17+ with `@Observable`):** `@State` - this view owns the value (a Bool, a String, or an `@Observable` model). Plain property (`let model: Model`) - read an observable model owned elsewhere; SwiftUI still tracks what you read. `@Binding` - a two-way link to someone else's value (a child toggle editing the parent's Bool). `@Bindable` - create bindings (`$model.name`) into an `@Observable` model. `@Environment` - read values or models injected high up (`.environment(model)`).

**The older set (`ObservableObject`, still in many apps):** `@StateObject` - owns the object; `@ObservedObject` - borrows it; `@EnvironmentObject` - injected; properties marked `@Published`. Drawback: any `@Published` change refreshes every view observing the object.
**Real-life analogy:** `@State` is your own notebook. `@Binding` is a friend letting you write in their notebook. `@Environment` is the notice board everyone in the building can read.
keyPoints: Ownership decides the wrapper: own → `@State`; borrow read-write → `@Binding`; injected → `@Environment`.
With `@Observable`, pass models as plain properties and use `@Bindable` for `$` bindings.
Legacy: `@StateObject` owns, `@ObservedObject` borrows; `@ObservedObject` for an owned object is a bug (recreated).
Keep `@State` private; it is internal to the view.
One source of truth per piece of data.

code.caption: Owner, child binding, bindable model

mistakes: Using `@ObservedObject var vm = ViewModel()` - the object is recreated whenever the parent redraws; use `@StateObject` (or `@State` with `@Observable`).
Initializing `@State` from an init parameter and expecting it to update when the parent changes - it is set only once.
Making `@State` non-private and setting it from outside.
followups: **`@StateObject` vs `@ObservedObject`?** StateObject creates and owns the object once for the view's lifetime; ObservedObject only observes an object owned elsewhere.
**How does a child change parent state?** Pass a `Binding` (`$value`) or a closure.
**Why is `@Observable` better than `ObservableObject`?** Views refresh only when a property they actually read changes.
